accepted.s:
Under Article 217 of the Constitution, a Judge of a High Court is appointed by the President after consultation with which of the following?
1. Chief Justice of India
2. Governor of the State
3. Chief Justice of the concerned High Court in the case of a puisne Judge
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The President appoints High Court Judges after consulting the CJI and the Governor; in the case of a puisne Judge, the Chief Justice of the concerned High Court is also consulted.
accepted.tq: Identify all constitutionally prescribed consultees and avoid confusing appointment with transfer.
accepted.sec: High Court judges - appointment, transfer, resignation, removal instances, writ and supervisory powers, contempt

accepted.s: In the present collegium procedure, the initial proposal for appointment of a High Court Judge is made by the Chief Justice of the High Court along with the High Court collegium consisting of the Chief Justice and:
o: All serving Judges of that High Court
accepted.x: The High Court collegium for initiating proposals consists of the Chief Justice and the two senior-most Judges of that High Court.
accepted.tq: Use the composition of the relevant collegium rather than the larger Supreme Court collegium.
accepted.sec: High Court judges - appointment, transfer, resignation, removal instances, writ and supervisory powers, contempt

accepted.s: The collegium at the Supreme Court level that examines proposals for appointment of High Court Judges comprises the Chief Justice of India and:
o: The two senior-most Judges of the concerned High Court
The four senior-most Judges of the Supreme Court
The two senior-most Judges of the Supreme Court
The Law Minister and two senior-most Judges of the Supreme Court
accepted.x: The Supreme Court collegium mentioned for these proposals consists of the CJI and the two senior-most Judges of the Supreme Court.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Supreme Court collegium from the High Court collegium and from executive consultation.
accepted.sec: High Court judges - appointment, transfer, resignation, removal instances, writ and supervisory powers, contempt

accepted.s: Who has the constitutional power to transfer a Judge from one High Court to another under Article 222?
o: The Governor after consulting the Chief Justice of India
The Union Law Minister after consulting the High Court collegium
The Chief Justice of India acting alone
The President after consulting the Chief Justice of India
accepted.x: A High Court Judge is transferred by the President after consultation with the Chief Justice of India.
accepted.tq: Ask who would perform the constitutional action and separate transfer from appointment.
accepted.sec: High Court judges - appointment, transfer, resignation, removal instances, writ and supervisory powers, contempt

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding removal of a High Court Judge:
1. Article 218 applies the Supreme Court Judge removal procedure to High Court Judges.
2. The procedure is governed by the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968.
3. A High Court Judge may be removed by the Governor through an executive order.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Articles 218 and the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968 provide the applicable removal framework. A Governor cannot remove a High Court Judge by executive order.
accepted.tq: Reject the wrong-authority trap and match the High Court procedure with the Supreme Court procedure.
accepted.sec: High Court judges - appointment, transfer, resignation, removal instances, writ and supervisory powers, contempt

accepted.s: Justice Soumitra Sen was associated with which of the following events?
o: He became the first Chief Justice of the Andhra Pradesh High Court
He resigned in 2011 after the Rajya Sabha voted for his removal
He was removed by the Governor of West Bengal
He was transferred from the Madras High Court to the Calcutta High Court
accepted.x: Justice Soumitra Sen of the Calcutta High Court resigned in 2011 after the Rajya Sabha voted for his removal.
accepted.tq: Match the judge with the specific removal-related event rather than the formal general procedure.
accepted.sec: High Court judges - appointment, transfer, resignation, removal instances, writ and supervisory powers, contempt

accepted.s:
With reference to recent proceedings concerning High Court Judges, consider the following statements:
1. A motion against Justice G.R. Swaminathan of the Madras High Court was noticed by 107 Members of Parliament in December 2025.
2. An inquiry report on Yashwant Varma was to be tabled despite his resignation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
accepted.x: Both statements are correct. The motion against Justice G.R. Swaminathan involved 107 MPs, and the inquiry report concerning Yashwant Varma was to be tabled despite his resignation.
accepted.tq: Check each recent factual detail independently before selecting the combined option.
accepted.sec: High Court judges - appointment, transfer, resignation, removal instances, writ and supervisory powers, contempt

accepted.s: Which one of the following best describes the scope of writ jurisdiction of a High Court under Article 226?
o: It extends only to disputes arising within the physical territory of the High Court
It is confined exclusively to enforcement of Fundamental Rights
It extends to Fundamental Rights and other legal rights, including where the cause of action arises within its territory
It can be exercised only on a reference from the Supreme Court
accepted.x: Article 226 enables High Courts to issue writs for Fundamental Rights and for any other purpose. A High Court may act even when the respondent is outside its territory if the cause of action arises within it.
accepted.tq: Contrast the wider wording of Article 226 with the narrower purpose traditionally associated with Article 32.
accepted.sec: High Court judges - appointment, transfer, resignation, removal instances, writ and supervisory powers, contempt

accepted.s: The inclusion of the power of High Courts to issue writs for ‘any other purpose’ makes Article 226 wider than Article 32 in respect of:
o: The power to amend the Constitution
The number of judges required to hear a petition
The range of rights that may be enforced
The power to remove constitutional authorities
accepted.x: Article 226 covers Fundamental Rights as well as other legal rights, whereas Article 32 is principally a remedy for enforcement of Fundamental Rights.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the purposes of Articles 226 and 32 by focusing on the phrase ‘any other purpose’.
accepted.sec: High Court judges - appointment, transfer, resignation, removal instances, writ and supervisory powers, contempt

accepted.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. 42nd Constitutional Amendment
B. 43rd Constitutional Amendment
C. 44th Constitutional Amendment
D. Contempt of Courts Act
accepted.x: The 42nd Amendment was enacted in 1976, the 43rd in 1977, the Contempt of Courts Act in 1971, and the 44th Amendment in 1978. Therefore, strictly by year the correct order is D, A, B, C.
accepted.tq: Check the dates of every item rather than relying on the apparent constitutional sequence.
accepted.sec: High Court judges - appointment, transfer, resignation, removal instances, writ and supervisory powers, contempt

accepted.s: The statement that High Courts exercise superintendence over all courts and tribunals within their territory, except military tribunals, refers to:
accepted.x: Article 227 confers on High Courts the power of superintendence over courts and tribunals within their territory, excluding military tribunals.
accepted.tq: Match the constitutional Article with its distinctive institutional power.
accepted.sec: High Court judges - appointment, transfer, resignation, removal instances, writ and supervisory powers, contempt

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 227:
1. It covers both administrative and judicial matters.
2. The High Court may exercise the power suo motu.
3. The Supreme Court possesses an identical power under Article 227.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Article 227 covers administrative and judicial superintendence and may be exercised suo motu. Article 227 is a High Court provision; the Supreme Court has no identical Article 227 power.
accepted.tq: Spot the institutional-body swap in the third statement.
accepted.sec: High Court judges - appointment, transfer, resignation, removal instances, writ and supervisory powers, contempt

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
o: Article 215 — High Courts as courts of record
Article 226 — Salaries of High Court Judges
Article 218 — Contempt jurisdiction of High Courts
accepted.x: Article 215 declares every High Court to be a court of record. Article 226 concerns writs, Article 227 superintendence, and Article 233 appointment of district judges.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure Article–subject pair and eliminate nearby constitutional provisions.
accepted.sec: High Court judges - appointment, transfer, resignation, removal instances, writ and supervisory powers, contempt

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of the appellate jurisdiction of a High Court mentioned in the constitutional scheme?
o: The High Court is primarily a court of appeal
A death sentence awarded by a Sessions Court requires High Court confirmation
Second civil appeals are confined to questions of law
Every factual finding of a subordinate court must be reconsidered in every second appeal
accepted.x: A second civil appeal is limited to a substantial question of law; there is no requirement that every factual finding be reconsidered. The other three describe features of High Court appellate work.
accepted.tq: Find the statement that exaggerates a limited appellate power into an absolute one.
accepted.sec: High Court judges - appointment, transfer, resignation, removal instances, writ and supervisory powers, contempt

accepted.s: The requirement that a death sentence awarded by a Sessions Court must be confirmed by the High Court is presently governed in the criminal procedural framework by the:
accepted.x: The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 replaced the Code of Criminal Procedure from 1 July 2024 and contains the relevant criminal procedure framework.
accepted.tq: Use the current statutory replacement rather than the repealed procedural code.

accepted.s: The Contempt of Courts Act, 1971 was enacted pursuant to the recommendations of the:
accepted.x: The Contempt of Courts Act, 1971 followed the report of the H.N. Sanyal Committee.
accepted.tq: Associate the statute with the committee that directly preceded it.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes civil contempt from criminal contempt?
o: Civil contempt is confined to inaccurate reporting, while criminal contempt covers fair criticism
Civil contempt is punishable only by the Governor, while criminal contempt is punishable only by Parliament
Civil contempt concerns only contempt of the Supreme Court, while criminal contempt concerns only High Courts
Civil contempt involves wilful disobedience, while criminal contempt includes scandalising or obstructing the administration of justice
accepted.x: Civil contempt includes wilful disobedience of a judgment, order or undertaking. Criminal contempt includes acts such as scandalising the court or obstructing the administration of justice.
accepted.tq: Compare the operative definitions instead of confusing the two categories by the court involved.
accepted.sec: High Court judges - appointment, transfer, resignation, removal instances, writ and supervisory powers, contempt

accepted.s: Which of the following is recognised as an exception or safeguard in contempt jurisdiction?
o: Wilful disobedience of a court order
Obstruction of the administration of justice
accepted.x: Fair criticism and accurate reporting are recognised exceptions or safeguards; wilful disobedience, obstruction and scandalising conduct may constitute contempt.
accepted.tq: Identify the legally protected expression among acts that can constitute contempt.
accepted.sec: High Court judges - appointment, transfer, resignation, removal instances, writ and supervisory powers, contempt

accepted.s: The Restatement of Values of Judicial Life adopted in 1997 consists of:
accepted.x: The 1997 Restatement of Values of Judicial Life contains 16 points.
accepted.tq: Use the exact numerical figure rather than the nearby constitutional and statutory dates.

accepted.s: The in-house procedure relating to judicial ethics was formulated in:

accepted.s: In September 2026, the Supreme Court refused to stay contempt proceedings of the Bombay High Court relating to:
o: A dispute over the appointment of a district judge
A disagreement over the transfer of a High Court Judge
A challenge to the Gram Nyayalayas Act
A Maharashtra judicial officer’s courtroom outburst
accepted.x: The proceedings concerned a courtroom outburst by a Maharashtra judicial officer, and the Supreme Court refused to stay the Bombay High Court contempt proceedings.
accepted.tq: Link the recent judicial event with the conduct that triggered the proceeding.

accepted.s: Under Article 233, a person seeking appointment as a District Judge from outside the judicial service must have been an advocate or pleader for at least:
accepted.x: Article 233 requires at least seven years’ standing as an advocate or pleader for such appointment.
accepted.tq: Recall the statutory threshold and distinguish it from longer judicial-service experience requirements.
accepted.sec: Subordinate judiciary - Article 233, AIJS, Lok Adalats, Gram Nyayalayas, mobile courts

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding appointment of District Judges under Article 233:
1. The Governor appoints District Judges in consultation with the High Court.
2. A person already in the service of the Union or the State is eligible for direct appointment under Article 233 merely on completing seven years as an advocate.
3. The provision requires seven years’ standing as an advocate or pleader for a person appointed from outside the judicial service.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Governor appoints District Judges in consultation with the High Court, and the seven-year advocacy requirement applies to a person from outside the judicial service. Mere completion of seven years as an advocate does not make a serving government employee eligible under this route.
accepted.tq: Use the eligibility exception to detect the overbroad statement.
accepted.sec: Subordinate judiciary - Article 233, AIJS, Lok Adalats, Gram Nyayalayas, mobile courts

accepted.s: Which one of the following constitutional provisions deals with the appointment of judicial officers other than District Judges?
accepted.x: Article 234 concerns recruitment of persons other than District Judges to the judicial service of a State.
accepted.tq: Separate the provision for District Judges from the provision for other judicial officers.
accepted.sec: Subordinate judiciary - Article 233, AIJS, Lok Adalats, Gram Nyayalayas, mobile courts

accepted.s: For appointment of judicial officers other than District Judges under Article 234, the Governor makes rules after consultation with the:
o: State Election Commission and Legislative Council
High Court collegium and Union Law Commission
State Public Service Commission and High Court
Union Public Service Commission and Supreme Court
accepted.x: Article 234 requires consultation with the State Public Service Commission and the High Court.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct combination of State-level recruiting authority and constitutional judicial authority.
accepted.sec: Subordinate judiciary - Article 233, AIJS, Lok Adalats, Gram Nyayalayas, mobile courts

accepted.s: The control over district courts and courts subordinate thereto, including postings, promotions and leave, is vested in the High Court under:
accepted.x: Article 235 vests control over district and subordinate courts in the High Court, including matters such as postings, promotions and leave.
accepted.tq: Match the administrative control function with its constitutional Article.
accepted.sec: Subordinate judiciary - Article 233, AIJS, Lok Adalats, Gram Nyayalayas, mobile courts

accepted.s: Which of the following is included within the constitutional meaning of ‘District Judge’ under Article 236?
o: City civil court judges and additional, joint and assistant district judges
All members of the Supreme Court
accepted.x: Article 236 includes judges of a city civil court and additional, joint and assistant district judges within the expression ‘District Judge’.
accepted.tq: Test the inclusive constitutional definition rather than the ordinary administrative meaning.
accepted.sec: Subordinate judiciary - Article 233, AIJS, Lok Adalats, Gram Nyayalayas, mobile courts

accepted.s: Under Article 237, the Governor may direct that the provisions relating to subordinate judiciary shall apply to:
accepted.x: Article 237 enables the Governor to apply the relevant provisions to magistrates in the State.
accepted.tq: Associate the enabling provision with the specific category of officers named in it.
accepted.sec: Subordinate judiciary - Article 233, AIJS, Lok Adalats, Gram Nyayalayas, mobile courts

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the position of a District Judge in the district judicial hierarchy?
o: The District Judge is subordinate to the District Magistrate in judicial matters
The District Judge hears only constitutional writ petitions
The District Judge is the highest civil court of the district and also functions as Sessions Judge in criminal matters
The District Judge is the lowest criminal court of the district
accepted.x: The District Judge is the highest civil court in the district and also exercises the powers of a Sessions Judge in criminal matters.
accepted.tq: Combine the civil and criminal roles instead of treating the District Judge as belonging to only one jurisdiction.
accepted.sec: Subordinate judiciary - Article 233, AIJS, Lok Adalats, Gram Nyayalayas, mobile courts

accepted.s: An appeal from the District Court ordinarily lies to the:
accepted.x: The ordinary appellate chain mentioned is District Court to High Court.
accepted.tq: Trace the appellate hierarchy from the subordinate court to the constitutional court above it.
accepted.sec: Subordinate judiciary - Article 233, AIJS, Lok Adalats, Gram Nyayalayas, mobile courts

accepted.s: The All India Judicial Service is constitutionally enabled by:
o: Article 312, as amended by the 42nd Amendment
Article 233, as amended by the 44th Amendment
Article 235, as amended by the 20th Amendment
Article 368, as amended by the 43rd Amendment
accepted.x: Article 312, as amended by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment, enables the creation of an All India Judicial Service. It has not yet been created.
accepted.tq: Match the service with both its enabling Article and the relevant constitutional amendment.
accepted.sec: Subordinate judiciary - Article 233, AIJS, Lok Adalats, Gram Nyayalayas, mobile courts

accepted.s: Which of the following is a principal issue in the debate over the All India Judicial Service?
o: Uniform merit-based recruitment versus State and High Court control and local-language needs
Replacement of civil courts by Lok Adalats in every case
Appointment of Governors versus election of Governors
Abolition of the Supreme Court versus creation of military tribunals
accepted.x: The debate balances uniform merit-based recruitment against concerns relating to State and High Court control and the importance of local languages.
accepted.tq: Identify the two competing institutional considerations rather than an unrelated judicial reform.
accepted.sec: Subordinate judiciary - Article 233, AIJS, Lok Adalats, Gram Nyayalayas, mobile courts

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the present status of the All India Judicial Service?
o: It is constitutionally enabled but has not yet been created
It functions only in Union Territories
It was abolished by the 44th Amendment
It was created by the 42nd Amendment and is fully operational
accepted.x: The Constitution enables the All India Judicial Service through Article 312, but the service has not yet been created.
accepted.tq: Distinguish constitutional authorisation from actual implementation.
accepted.sec: Subordinate judiciary - Article 233, AIJS, Lok Adalats, Gram Nyayalayas, mobile courts

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes a Gram Nyayalaya?
o: It is presided over by a Nyayadhikari of JMFC rank and functions as a mobile court at the intermediate Panchayat level
It is presided over by a High Court Judge and hears only constitutional cases
It is a permanent bench of the Supreme Court in every village
It is presided over by the District Magistrate and hears only revenue disputes
accepted.x: A Gram Nyayalaya is presided over by a Nyayadhikari of Judicial Magistrate First Class rank and functions as a mobile court at the intermediate Panchayat level.
accepted.tq: Identify the institution through its presiding officer, level and mobile character.

accepted.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Article 233 — District Judges
2. Article 234 — Other judicial officers
3. Article 235 — High Court control over subordinate courts
4. Articles 236–237 — Definitions and extension to magistrates
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched: Articles 233, 234 and 235 deal respectively with District Judges, other judicial officers and High Court control; Articles 236–237 concern definitions and extension to magistrates.
accepted.tq: Build the constitutional sequence from Articles 233 to 237 and verify every pair.
